cases.question: What was the highest dispatch total demand (TOTALDEMAND) in Queensland across the whole of Wednesday 29 July 2026, Brisbane local time, and when did that peak happen?
cases.notes: QLD1 chosen: the brief excludes NSW1 and TAS1, and VIC1's 29 July 2026 day is development material (any measure). QLD1's development item for that day is operational demand only, so dispatch total demand on QLD1 is not development material. Window is fully held for total demand (288 of 288 five-minute intervals). QLD1 has no daylight saving, so the day is 24 hours at +10:00.

cases.question: For SA1, over the full local day of 29 July 2026 (midnight to midnight, Adelaide time), which 5-minute interval carried the day's top dispatch total demand, and what level did it hit?
cases.notes: SA1 chosen: with F01 = QLD1 and NSW1/TAS1 excluded, the only other candidate is VIC1, whose 29 July 2026 day is development material. The SA1 day itself is not development material, but it contains one development half-hour (SA1, ending 2026-07-29T08:00:00Z); this cannot be avoided because every remaining region's day is development material. Fully held: 288 of 288 intervals. Tests the +09:30 offset.

cases.question: Across New South Wales' whole local day, Wednesday 29 July 2026 by Sydney clocks from midnight to midnight, which half-hour saw the maximum operational demand, and what was the level?
cases.notes: NSW1 chosen: QLD1 is excluded by the brief, and TAS1/VIC1 29 July 2026 days are development material for any measure. NSW1's development item for that day is total demand only, so operational demand there is not listed. The day contains one development half-hour (NSW1, ending 2026-07-28T21:30:00Z); SA1, the only alternative, also contains one, so this cannot be avoided; NSW1 was preferred to spread regions (SA1 is already F02). Fully held: 48 of 48 half-hours.

cases.question: On Hobart clocks, covering the whole of Sunday 5 April 2026, how high did TAS1 operational demand peak and in which half-hour?
cases.notes: TAS1 chosen to spread regions; it observes daylight saving, which ended on 5 April 2026, so the local day is 25 hours (50 half-hours, all held). No development material covers April 2026. The question deliberately does not mention the 25-hour length, so the assistant must work it out.

cases.question: Within the request's window for NSW1 (2 pm to 9 pm AEDT, Sydney daylight time, on Saturday 4 April 2026), find the maximum operational demand and report the half-hour it was recorded in.
cases.notes: Explicit 7-hour window on half-hour boundaries, inside the NSW1 operational-demand held range 2026-04-03T18:00Z to 2026-04-05T18:00Z (14 of 14 half-hours held). Not a whole local day or an event window. Words match the fields: 2 pm and 9 pm AEDT (+11:00, daylight saving still in force on 4 April) are 03:00Z and 10:00Z. Operational demand is used here so that F06 can use total demand. No development material covers April 2026.

cases.question: Thinking about the Victorian high-price event of 20 August 2026, how high did VIC1 dispatch total demand (TOTALDEMAND) go over that event's full window, and when was the top reached?
cases.notes: Event VIC1-20260820T0910-hi: the only VIC1 event on 20 August 2026 and the only high-price event that day, so region + kind + date identify it uniquely. Not development material (unlike VIC1-20260728T2120-lo, SA1-20260731T0235-hi and the TAS1 6 August day; NSW1-20260731T0730-hi and SA1-20260729T1755-hi contain development half-hours). Fully held for total demand: 294 of 294 intervals. Identified by date rather than peak time so the question carries no time that might coincide with the answer.

cases.question: Based only on data published by noon Brisbane time on Sunday 5 October 2025, what was the highest operational demand in Queensland over that entire local day, and at what time?
cases.notes: QLD1 local day 5 October 2025 (fully held, 48 half-hours; not development material; 24 hours since QLD1 has no daylight saving). Cutoff 2025-10-05T02:00:00Z = noon AEST, strictly inside the window. By the cutoff 8 half-hours have a public row (published 2025-10-04T21:26Z) and 40 do not (earliest publication 2025-10-05T21:26Z), so the whole-day maximum cannot be established as of the cutoff. The question asks for the whole day's maximum and names the cutoff in words that match the field.

cases.question: During Tasmania's 31 July 2026 high-price episode, how far did demand climb and when did it top out?
cases.notes: Names no measure (only 'demand'), so a careful assistant must ask whether dispatch total demand or operational demand is meant. Otherwise in scope: TAS1, and the window of event TAS1-20260731T0730-hi (the only TAS1 event on 31 July 2026), which is fully held for both measures (288/288 and 48/48), so the missing measure is the only defect. Not development material.
